posts.author: supah
posts.body: Although I've been using RPG Maker MV for a long time now, I'm still fairly new to it. I am wondering, is it possible to make the tilesets larger? I am making a joke game about a mop named Borkles (because my more serious project is on hiatus, I need to work on something more simple) and his sprites dimensions are 96x96, which looks weird with the small tiles. Is there any way I can make this look better or do I have to downsize Borkles to 48x48 (which I don't like)? I also plan on making my own tiles (if I can figure out how to without getting overwhelmed) instead of using the default RPG Maker MV tilesets. which are just placeholders.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Technically yes, but also no.
The editor cannot be modified; plugins can only modify how the game itself operates, but not how the editor operates. The MV editor does not natively support different tile sizes, so basically it can only represent 48x48 tiles.
That said, there are some plugins, such as
Shaz's Change Tile Size plugin
, but in this case, you'll be required to keep the original 48x48 tiles so that the editor can see them (and therefore you can see them), but when you launch the game it will read the tileset from a different folder. It's sort of a hacky work around.
For a bit of opinion; I mean derpy MS paint doodle aside, nothing looks off about the size to me. Looking at the wood veneer on my own floor I'd say a mop head covers about 3 panels which looks pretty close to what your image shows.
edit:
as an alternative, you could do the 48x48 character sprite and then just use a map zoom plugin to zoom in 2x. That seems messier and comes with it's own fair share of problems, but figured it was worth throwing it out there for your consideration.
